title: ops-watchbook-metrics-trace-lexicon-and-widget-playlist
summary: A compact, operational playbook intended for oncall and dashboard owners that defines a shared lexicon of key inference metrics, a trace anchoring strategy, and a prioritized "widget playlist" for small, cost-aware operator dashboards. Focused on enabling rapid investigation of tail-latency and cache/cold-start behaviors while keeping query costs bounded.
body:
Purpose:
This is an operational watchbook for SREs, oncall engineers, and dashboard owners. It defines consistent metric names and calculations, prescribes trace-anchor patterns for multi-hop inference flows, and proposes a lightweight widget playlist (ordered) that provides the 80/20 investigation surface for regressions during rollouts or incidents.

Audience:
- Oncall engineers and rotation leads
- Observability dashboard owners and curators
- Feature/product teams running model rollouts or canary experiments

Scope and constraints:
- Surface-level: request-to-first-token (TTFT), streaming tail, KV cache warmth, routing fallback counts, batch-size histogram, and token-economics approximations.
- Cost constraint: widgets and probes must be bounded to a combined query budget per workspace (see "widget-budget") to avoid runaway cost during high-cardinality investigation windows.

Guiding principles (short):
1) Per-session provenance: prefer a single session_id that stitches trace spans across API, router, model tasks, and cache layers.
2) Progressive fidelity: dashboards show coarse summary metrics by default with drilldowns that enable sample-driven traces.
3) Cost-awareness: sample traces adaptively and limit full-record traces to critical-error buckets.
4) Actionability: every alert surface links to a triage playbook with a small set of next steps.

Metric lexicon (name | unit | calc | owner | rationale):
- request.p95_first_token_ms | ms | 95th percentile of (t_first_token - t_request_received) per 5m window | owner: obs-runtime | Rationale: customer-perceived latency for streaming workloads.
- request.p99_end_to_end_ms | ms | 99th percentile of (t_last_token_emitted - t_request_received) per 5m | owner: obs-runtime | Rationale: captures long tail interactive sessions.
- kvcache.warmth_index | ratio [0-1] | (hits / (hits + misses)) over rolling 1h by model+tenant | owner: serving-kv | Rationale: quick signal for cold-cache effects across tenants.
- routing.fallback_rate | pct | (fallback_calls / total_calls) * 100 per 5m by route | owner: routing | Rationale: detect degraded capacity or policy-triggered fallbacks.
- batch.size_median | tokens/request | median batch size for inference kernels per 5m | owner: serving-runtime | Rationale: helps detect batching degradation that impacts latency or cost.
- token.econ_per_1000 | USD approximation | estimated token cost per 1000 tokens using current quantization profile and GPU cost model | owner: cost-ops | Rationale: surface unit economics drift during rollouts.
- model.quality_regressions | count | number of eval-prompt mismatches flagged by quality probes per 1h | owner: ml-quality | Rationale: early detection of silent regressions (e.g., truncation/quantization issues).

Alerting guidance (threshold examples):
- request.p95_first_token_ms > 350ms for 3 consecutive 1m buckets -> P2 alert (latency impact)
- kvcache.warmth_index drops below 0.35 for >10m for >10% of heavy tenants -> P1 if correlated with p99 latency rise
- routing.fallback_rate > 5% sustained for 15m -> P1 (possible capacity/region degradation)
Notes: thresholds are templates; teams owning dashboards should tune by model class and SLAs.

Trace anchoring strategy (how to structure spans):
1) Root span: api.request (attributes: tenant_id, route_id, session_id, client_version, request_size_tokens)
2) Router span(s): router.decision (attributes: selected_pool, fallback_reason, policy_version)
3) Inference spans: model.exec.chunk_N (attributes: model_name, quant_profile, seq_length, batch_size, kernel_variant)
4) KV cache spans: kv.check, kv.fetch, kv.prefetch (attributes: key_count, hit/miss)
5) Egress/stream spans: stream.emit_chunk (attributes: chunk_size_tokens, emit_latency_ms)
Anchoring rules:
- Always record the session_id and a small sampling trace_id in metrics for correlation.
- Use severity_score tag on traces when a metric crosses a threshold (e.g., severity=latency-high).
- Prefer lightweight logs in spans and avoid including full prompt text except in guarded, redacted sampled traces (compliance).

Sampling policy (adaptive):
- Default: 0.5% trace sampling for successful requests across production.
- Elevated sample: When request.p99_end_to_end_ms > baseline*2 for a route, automatically increase sampling for that route to 10% for 30 minutes.
- Error sample: All requests that triggered fallback_rate decisions or model.quality_regressions are sampled at 100% for the next 15 minutes.
- Cost cap: aggregate trace retention per tenant must not exceed widget-budget (see below); if budget is hit, reduce default sampling first.

Widget playlist (priority ordered):
1) Ops Overview Sparkline Row (always-on): p50/p90/p95/p99 latency and request rate, sketch of kvcache.warmth_index, fallback_rate.
2) Tail Heatmap (30m window): per-route p99 broken into bucketed causes (kv miss, large batch, model-run).
3) Session Slicer (top-20): session-level mini-table with request_id, user_tenant, p99_latency, kv_warmth_at_request, routing_pool, trace_link.
4) Batch Distribution Histogram: shows kernel batch sizes with median and tail.
5) Cost Drift Panel: token.econ_per_1000 vs. expected baseline; annotate with recent quant_profile rollouts.
6) Probe Timeline (canary): probe results and quality_regressions count for active rollouts.
7) Trace Sampler Control: small form to trigger immediate high-fidelity sampling for a given route or tenant for 1h (requires approval tag).
Notes: Widget rows must be horizontally compressed to fit in compact ops layout; prefer micro-widgets that link to bigger drilldowns rather than full expanded queries.

Widget-budget (operational config):
- Default: dashboards under the "ops" workspace may spend up to 1,000 probe queries/day and up to 500 stored traces/day.
- Owners may request increase for short-lived experiments via OBS-1124 request flow.

Investigation playflow (quick):
1) Detect: alert triggers an ops-overview P95/99 spike.
2) Scope: open Session Slicer and filter to top heavy tenants; check kvcache.warmth_index and routing.fallback_rate.
3) Correlate: use trace links from session rows to inspect route.decision spans and model.exec spans to see kernel variant and batch sizes.
4) Mitigate: if fallback_rate is high, route traffic to fallback pool or lower burst concurrency; if kv warmth low, trigger targeted prefetch for top keys (prefetch policy documented in prefetch-playbook).
5) Postmortem: capture root causes into a triage card and mark any dashboard tuning required.

Operational TODOs (short list):
- [ ] Wire session_id into router decision logs (owner: router eng) — due 2026-01-30
- [ ] Implement adaptive sampling hook in trace-agent to honor trace_budget API (owner: obs-platform) — due 2026-02-12
- [ ] Add token.econ_per_1000 annotation to rollout dashboard (owner: cost-ops) — due 2026-01-20
- [ ] Draft a small runbook linking widget playlist to specific remediation playbooks (owner: Asha) — due 2026-01-19

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs:
- Prompt redaction policy: should sampled traces include redacted prompt segments for quality debugging? (privacy vs. quality visibility)
- Default thresholds: how to auto-derive baseline by model class vs. per-route SLA; consider ML-driven baselining.
- Widget ownership: what is the rotation cadence for dashboard owners to prune widgets and maintain query budgets?

Reference snippets and helpful links:
- GH issue for sampling hook: redwood/observability#482
- JIRA: OBS-1124 for trace budget increases
- Slack playground thread: #observability widget-playlist-discuss (pin: recommended panels)

Notes to self / working hypotheses (informal):
- Hypothesis A: sudden drop in kvcache.warmth_index correlates with platform autoscaler churn; quick synthetic prefetch probe after deploy may reduce p99 within 15m.
- Hypothesis B: batch.size_median drift upwards when a specific kernel_variant is selected; costly tail latency is driven by kernel inefficiency not tenant load.

History and change log:
- 2025-11-03: initial draft (Asha)
- 2025-12-08: added sampling policy and widget-budget (Marcus)
- 2026-01-12: tuned alert thresholds and added operational TODOs (Eve)

If you're reading this during an incident: prioritize the "Session Slicer" and the "Tail Heatmap" first, and tag "ops-escalation" in the trace when you save a sampled trace for postmortem.

End of watchbook.
